investor_summary:
## Key Drivers

• **HDFC Bank** — The bank submitted CEO candidates to the RBI and Macquarie highlighted an external hire as a potential re-rating catalyst, which triggered the stock's biggest intraday jump in four months. As one of the fund's largest holdings (about 7.6% of the portfolio), this rally meaningfully supported the week's positive performance.

• **Infosys and HCL Technologies** — Comments from Anthropic's CEO calling for a slower pace of AI development lifted IT stocks, with Infosys surging about 6% and HCL Tech up as much as 7%. Infosys's strong ADR performance reinforced the rally, and both are meaningful fund positions (roughly 3.3% and 4.2% of the portfolio), making this a key driver of the fund's gain.

• **ICICI Bank** — The stock fell for a fifth straight session amid continued selling pressure, with an intraday drop of 1.74% on the week's worst day. Rising FCNR(B) deposit costs also pointed to margin pressure for banks. As a large fund holding (about 5.7% of the portfolio), this decline was a partial offset to the week's gains.

• **Automobiles sector** — Passenger vehicle exports fell 17% in August, a bearish demand signal that weighed on the sector, which declined 3.16% for the week. With roughly 6.7% of the fund in this sector, the weakness acted as a partial offset to the overall gain.

• **Coal India** — The company came under pressure as the Coal Ministry denied supply shortages and data showed adequate coal stocks at Punjab power plants, reducing near-term shortage fears and weighing on coal stocks. The decline in this roughly 5% portfolio holding was another offset to the week's positive performance.

## Overall Summary

The fund finished the week slightly higher, driven by strong gains in two key areas. HDFC Bank rallied on optimism around its CEO succession process, while IT stocks including Infosys and HCL Technologies surged after a prominent call for slower AI development improved the sector's demand outlook. These gains were partially offset by weakness in ICICI Bank on margin concerns and a fifth straight session of selling, a 17% drop in passenger vehicle exports that pressured the Automobiles sector, and Coal India's decline as supply-shortage fears eased. Overall, the fund's large positions in HDFC Bank and the IT names outweighed the drag from banks and autos to deliver a modestly positive week.
